statement: Built to be co-developed with First Nations farmers; we'd only add a reserve field with the Nation's permission.

lower_river_nation.note: Salmon River 1 is the reserve on the lower Salmon River

engagement_steps: Contact Splatsin first: its reserve, Salmon River 1, is on the lower Salmon River. Its public lands page lists the Lands Department and the Territorial Water Manager role.
Send a short, plain-language note: what the tool does, that no reserve data has been analysed, and whether there is any interest at all. Accept "no" or no reply.
Ask for the Nation's research protocol and who decides. A Band Council Resolution or a data-sharing agreement may be needed.

Offer in writing: Nation ownership of all outputs for its land, co-design, no publication without written consent, data returned or deleted on request, credit and paid time, and a community-controlled version if wanted.
Expect months, not a hackathon weekend. Nothing is added before the answer is yes.
Talk to the neighbouring Nations and bodies with interests in the river (Neskonlith, Adams Lake, Okanagan Indian Band, Secwépemc Fisheries Commission).

principles.name: OCAP®
principles.description: Ownership, Control, Access and Possession: First Nations control data collection in their communities and own their information collectively. OCAP® is a registered trademark of the First Nations Information Governance Centre (FNIGC).

principles.name: CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance
principles.description: Collective benefit, Authority to control, Responsibility and Ethics (Global Indigenous Data Alliance); they complement the FAIR data principles.

principles.name: TCPS 2 (2022), Chapter 9
principles.description: Research involving First Nations, Inuit and Métis Peoples: Art. 9.1 requires seeking community engagement, including for research on First Nations lands.

water_timeline.title: Fish population protection order M0238_2023 (lower Salmon River; M0239_2023 for Bessette Creek): about 398 surface and groundwater licence holders stop using water for forage crops.
Low-flow monitoring: the Secwépemc Fisheries Commission and Splatsin's Yucwmenlúcwu (caretakers of the land) staff assessed low-flow barriers to fish passage on the lower Salmon River.
Temporary protection order issued for the Salmon River.
Order rescinded as farmers and ranchers dealt with elevated wildfire risk (BC's wording).
Okanagan Nation Chiefs Executive Council letter to the Minister about the order being rescinded without consultation.

New temporary protection order: 458 surface water and groundwater licences and transitioning groundwater users in the Salmon River watershed stop irrigating forage crops, lawns, fairways and gardens; effective 19 Aug 2026.
